children: Boeing Company (NYSE:BA) is expanding military and commercial reach—winning a boosted $19.1B USAF ceiling including FMS and a role on the F-47, landing record deliveries and net orders YTD, securing a tentative SPEEA labor deal, forecasting strong Africa growth, as NTSB probes a fatal 767 overrun.
: U.S. Air Force raised Boeing (BA) contract ceiling to $19.1B from $5.7B, adding foreign military sales (initially Japan, Israel). Work in Seattle; expected completion April 28, 2035.
: Boeing Company (BA) delivered 418 airplanes year-to-date through August 2026, the highest through August since 2018, and recorded 453 net orders year-to-date after accounting for cancellations.
: Boeing (BA) won a 2025 contract for the U.S. Air Force’s sixth‑generation fighter (F‑47), joining Northrop Grumman. Contract work and related deliveries are expected in coming years.

: Boeing (BA) reached a tentative four-year contract with SPEEA covering ~17,000 engineers/techs: 10% raise Oct 16, then 4% annual raises plus merit increases 2027–2030; updated WFH and overtime rules

: NTSB says pilots of an Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 considered aborting a Miami landing after a runway overrun that killed five; investigators will interview pilots and release cockpit voice recorder.
: Boeing forecasts Africa passenger traffic to grow ~5.8–6% annually to mid-2040s, RPKs near 1 trillion, fleet rising from 715 (2024) to ~1,680 by 2044; single-aisles and widebodies expand.
This is an AI-generated summary and may contain inaccuracies. Please verify any important information with the original sources.

title: Weekly Recap: U.S. Air Force $19.1B ceiling and 418 deliveries, 453 orders
